In the hallway and the living room the wheels hardly slip, and the history only shows that there is enough traction. At the turn into the kitchen they do slip, but from a few steps with noisy sensors it's hard to tell carpet from a slightly worse floor. The module learned on the mean squared error, and in such cases it outputs the average over similar floors; since a traction of 1 is the highest of those seen in training, that average is lower. This doesn't hurt the driving: with this estimate, Ada makes it on ${pct(r.rmaOk)}% of test drives on carpet, in ${sec(r.rmaTime)} on average, and the teacher with the true μ on ${pct(r.tOk)}%, in ${sec(r.tTime)}. The RMA authors write the same: the estimate doesn't need to be correct in some “ground truth” sense; what matters is that it leads to the right action.
